newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel, Palestinians set up Gaza "no-go" areas.
newsitem.headline: Israel, Palestinians set up Gaza "no-go" areas.

text.p: The Israeli army said on Friday it had agreed with Palestinian police to set up 300-metre (yard)-deep buffer zones around Israeli outposts in the Gaza Strip where Arab demonstrators will not be allowed to set foot.

"On the orders of the chief of the Israeli army's southern command, military commanders toured possible points of friction in the Gaza Strip with their Palestinian police colleagues," an army spokeswoman said.

"To reduce this friction and prevent another escalation of (violence), they agreed on and marked security areas of about 300 metres where Palestinian police will prevent the entry of demonstrators," she said.
The spokeswoman said similar arrangements had yet to be established in the West Bank.

Since Israel's opening last week of an entrance to a controversial archaeological tunnel in Arab East Jerusalem, 73 Palestinians and Israelis have been killed in clashes in the West Bank and Gaza Strip.
Some Palestinian policemen took part in the gun battles.
Under interim deals on Palestinian self-rule, Jewish settlements and Israeli soldiers remain in many parts of both areas pending a final peace accord.
Israeli and Palestinian negotiators are due to resume peace talks on Sunday at the Erez border crossing between Israel and Gaza following this week's emergency Middle East summit in Washington.
